title: HelioPort model synthesis and toolchain scout
summary: Introductory discovery to map HelioPort's ingestion and TMS integration needs; primary constraints are low-latency routing for live dispatch, large context windows for multimodal manifests, and strict data residency. We discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, model candidates (open Llama-family, Mistral, Redmond-style variants), multilingual and tool-calling support for their TMS API and external shipment tracking, and a pilot plan for a Dedicated reserve with a 3-week POC for latency benchmarks.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Dedicated sizing estimate + 3-week POC pricing by 2027-03-12
Liam Patel: Share internal benchmarking notes on 32k vs 64k context models and KV cache tuning (link) by 2027-03-11
Markus Li: Provide sample manifest and representative request traces (anonymized) by 2027-03-10
Priya Kapoor: Confirm regulatory regions (EU, US) and whether data residency required by 2027-03-09
next_steps: Redwood to propose Dedicated pilot plan + SLA targets
Customer to send sample payloads and latency SLAs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-08
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (HelioPort CTO), Priya Kapoor (Head of AI), Markus Li (SRE), Sofia Morales (Product)

Summary (autogenerated, may be rough): discussed model candidates, context windows, tool-calling patterns for TMS, hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, compliance notes.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Daniel: Doing well, Maya, thanks. We wanted to get into how Redwood can help with, uh, our dispatch AI — low latency on the edge of our TMS and supporting long manifests.
[00:15] Priya: Yep, and multilingual — we need English, Spanish, Portuguese support for LATAM routes. Also curious about tool-calling to our internal TMS APIs.
[00:22] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick plan: we'll do a high-level qualification, then drill into model/context needs and the networking options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). I'll also sketch how tool-calling and KV/prefix caching could work for you.
[00:32] Sofia: Quick note — Markus is our SRE and will ask infra questions.
[00:36] Markus: Yep. We care about VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs; also wondering about egress patterns for shipment-tracking calls.

[05:05] Liam: Can you describe a typical request? You mentioned manifests — what's the typical token length and request pattern?
[05:11] Priya: A full manifest can be pretty big — like 8k to 25k tokens depending on attachments or OCR text. For route planning we sometimes need the last day's context, so that's where we worry about longer context windows.
[05:25] Maya: Got it, so there's both single-request size and session/history. On the model front, are you aiming to tune an open model or are you open to Redwood-curated variants?
[05:34] Daniel: We prefer open models for license flexibility, but we need strong multilingual performance and low latency for inference in production. Cost matters but not at the expense of missing SLAs.

[07:45] Liam: For long context and multilingual, we usually look at these axes: (1) model architecture (Mistral-ish vs Llama-derivatives), (2) quantization and kernel support, (3) runtime features like continuous KV caching and prefix cache. In practice, 32k context is common, 64k for the heaviest manifests. We can route heavy contexts to Dedicated nodes optimized for large sequence kernels to keep latency stable.
[08:12] Markus: That sentence on routing — so you can steer requests to different capacity tiers automatically?
[08:17] Liam: Yeah, policy-based routing — latency SLO, cost cap, region, and model-compatibility are used to pick the target. For example, short chat can go to hosted smaller models, big manifests go to dedicated GPU with 64k kernels.
[08:28] Markus: Does that require a VPC? We want traffic to stay within our network for PII.
[08:33] Maya: You can use Redwood Private with our customer-managed control plane in your VPC or run an on-prem package. Dedicated also supports VPC peering and private networking for egress control.

[11:50] Priya: Tool-calling — we need the model to be able to call our TMS to pull live shipment status and to post suggested reroutes. How secure is that?
[11:58] Liam: Tool-calling is done over authenticated APIs; you can put the calling endpoint inside your VPC and we support per-call credentials, signed tokens, and option to truncate responses. We also support granular RBAC for who can call which tool.
[12:10] Daniel: Any examples of customers doing this for low-latency autopilot for routing?
[12:14] Maya: Yes — a logistics customer in EMEA uses Dedicated with an internal TMS and they run a 50ms median extra hop for tool calls; exact numbers depend on your topology though. We can run a bench for HelioPort.

[15:40] Markus: On encryption — KMS/HSM support? We need separation of keys and audit logs to satisfy our auditor.
[15:46] Liam: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations, plus audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. Dedicated can also integrate with your KMS in many cases; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we have SOC/ISO attestations.
[15:58] Markus: Are audit logs redactable? We don't want raw PII in long-term logs.
[16:02] Maya: You can configure PII redaction and retention windows per project. We'll share the security pack with specifics.

[19:20] Priya: Performance: if we pick a 64k model (open), what's a reasonable per-token latency baseline on Dedicated GPUs?
[19:27] Liam: On optimized kernels with batch size 1 and continuous KV, you're looking at something like 40–80ms per 1k tokens for generation tail, but that varies a lot — prompt prep, network, and tool-calls add overhead. For heavy manifests the trick is prefix caching: we cache model encodings for repeated prefixes to cut inference time significantly.
[19:47] Daniel: Can Redwood do prefix caching across sessions? We have templates that repeat a lot.
[19:51] Liam: Yes — automatic prefix/KV cache across shards. You can also pin frequently used prefixes to keep warm.

[23:10] Sofia: Cost question — what's the cost delta roughly between Hosted and Dedicated for our expected throughput?
[23:16] Maya: Hosted has lower operational fuss but higher per-token costs for sustained high throughput. Dedicated is CAPEX/commit style with lower unit costs if you run steady. We'll model your numbers in the estimate.

[25:00] Priya: We also need support for Spanish/Portuguese code-switching when drivers switch languages mid-message — how do models handle that?
[25:07] Liam: Some open models are better at multilingual; you might want a small ensemble approach — use a multilingual base model for parsing and a tuned variant for generation in target language. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and model mix.

[28:55] Daniel: About regulatory regions — we need EU residency for GDPR-sensitive manifests. Can we keep logs in EU-only?
[29:00] Maya: Yes, Dedicated or Private with region pinning can restrict storage/processing to EU. Hosted has region options but for strict residency Dedicated/Private is the recommended path.

[31:40] Markus: Operational — what's the upgrade/rollout story for model versions? We need canary deploys and rollback if quality regresses.
[31:47] Liam: Redwood supports canary/A-B rollouts, automatic fallback policies to a compatible model variant, and evaluation hooks linked to your prompt set so regressions trigger alerts.

[35:05] Priya: For the POC, we'd like to measure end-to-end p99 latency for a typical reroute flow including a TMS tool call and then generation — aim for under 350ms p99. Feasible?
[35:15] Liam: It's aggressive but possible with Dedicated nodes colocated in your region and synchronous tool-call optimizations. We'll need your traces and to run bench tests.

[38:50] Maya: A few admin things — we'll need to build an SOW for the POC, a proposed schedule, and a pricing sketch for a small Dedicated pool for three weeks. I'll own that and send it by Friday.
[39:01] Daniel: Great. Also want references — can you share a logistics case study?
[39:05] Maya: Yes, will attach a redacted case study and a short benchmark deck. Link: https://redwood.example/decks/helioport-pilot-template.pdf

[41:30] Sofia: Any gotchas — third-party libraries or tool-calling latencies that have surprised customers?
[41:36] Liam: Often it's network egress and synchronous HTTP timeouts; batching too aggressively can hurt latency; and some models need kernel-level tuning for 64k. We keep a library of optimized kernels but sometimes require a short tuning pass.

[44:10] Priya: Competitors question — we are also talking to MegaCloud AI and a smaller vendor (Infera). What would you say differentiates Redwood?
[44:18] Maya: We try to be production-first: transparent perf profiles, model rollout tooling, and unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We also focus on cost controls — batching and caching levers that materially cut per-token costs without sacrificing SLAs.

[47:05] Daniel: Ok, recap and next steps?
[47:09] Maya: Recap: Redwood will send Dedicated sizing & pricing + POC SOW; Liam will share kernel/context tuning notes; HelioPort will send sample manifests and traces and confirm EU residency requirement. We'll schedule the SE deep-dive week of 2027-03-15.
[47:22] Priya: Sounds good.
[47:25] Markus: I'll put together anonymized traces and the network diagram.

[50:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[50:03] Daniel: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription may contain imperfect names/terms (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), occasional filler words, and minor overlaps. Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example/decks/helioport-pilot-template.pdf , security pack link: https://redwood.example/security/pack.pdf
